q.t: Congruent figures have…
o: the same shape and the same size
q.e: Congruent figures can be placed one on the other to fit exactly.

q.t: What single measurement fixes a circle exactly?
q.e: All circles with the same radius are congruent.

q.t: Which is NOT a congruence condition for triangles?
q.e: Equal angles can come in different sizes — a small and a large triangle.

q.t: In a right triangle, the side opposite the right angle is called the…
q.e: The hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the 90° angle.

q.t: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is…
q.e: Angles opposite equal sides are equal, so all three are equal and share 180°.

q.t: When checking congruence, may you flip a figure over?
o: Yes — sliding, turning and flipping are allowed
q.e: A flipped copy still has the same shape and size.

q.t: Two triangles have all three sides equal. Which rule shows they are congruent?
q.e: Side-Side-Side.

q.t: In isosceles ∆ABC, AB = AC and ∠A = 80°. Find ∠B.
q.e: ∠B = ∠C (opposite equal sides). 180 − 80 = 100, shared equally → 50°.

q.t: If ∆ABC ≅ ∆XYZ, which side equals BC?
q.e: Second and third letters B, C match second and third letters Y, Z.

q.t: In a triangle, angles opposite equal sides are…
q.e: Shown with congruent halves (RHS) in an isosceles triangle.

q.t: ∆ABC ≅ ∆XYZ. Which other statement is also correct?
q.e: Both names must be reordered the same way so A–X, B–Y, C–Z still match.

q.t: Two sides and the angle BETWEEN them are equal. Which rule?
q.e: Side-Angle-Side, with the angle included between the two sides.

q.t: Why does SSA not guarantee congruence?
o: The arc can cut the line at two points, giving two different triangles
q.e: The side opposite the given angle can swing to two positions — a thin and a fat triangle.

q.t: ∠A = 35°, ∠C = 75° in ∆ABC. Find ∠B.
q.e: Angle sum: 180 − 110 = 70°. This is how AAS becomes ASA.

q.t: A is the centre of a circle, B and C are on it, ∠BAC = 120°. Find ∠ABC.
q.e: AB = AC are radii, so ∠B = ∠C = (180 − 120) ÷ 2 = 30°.

q.t: What fixes a rectangle exactly?
q.e: All angles are 90° anyway; length and breadth fix everything else.

q.t: O is the midpoint of both AD and BC. Which rule shows ∆AOB ≅ ∆DOC?
o: SAS — with vertically opposite angles at O
q.e: AO = OD, BO = OC and ∠AOB = ∠DOC (vertically opposite) — the angle is between the two sides.

q.t: AB = AD and CB = CD in a kite ABCD. Why is ∆ABC ≅ ∆ADC?
o: SSS — AC is a shared side
q.e: Three pairs of equal sides: AB = AD, CB = CD, AC = AC.

q.t: Two right triangles have equal hypotenuses and one other equal side. They are…
q.e: The right angle makes the two possible positions mirror images, so they are congruent.

q.t: Triangles with angles 30°, 70°, 80° — are they all congruent?
o: No — they can be different sizes
Only if drawn on the same page
Only if the 80° angle is at the top
q.e: Same angles give the same shape but not necessarily the same size.

q.t: ∆HEN ≅ ∆BIG. Which is also correct?
q.e: Reverse both: H–B, E–I, N–G still pair up.

q.t: AB = EF, ∠A = ∠E, AC = ED. The congruence is…
q.e: A–E (the angles); B–F because AB = EF; C–D because AC = ED.

q.t: AB = DF, ∠B = ∠F, AC = DE. Are the triangles definitely congruent?
q.e: ∠B is not between sides AB and AC, so it's the unreliable SSA case.

q.t: ∠A = ∠D, ∠B = ∠E, AC = DF. Which rule applies?
q.e: Two angles and a side that is not between them → AAS (the third angle also matches, so it's really ASA).

q.t: In rectangle ABCD with diagonal BD, which statement is correct?
q.e: AB must sit on CD and AD on CB: A↔C, B↔D, D↔B.

q.t: ∠B = 90° = ∠D, AB = DF, AC = FE. The congruence is…
q.e: B–D (right angles), A–F (AB = DF), C–E (hypotenuses AC = FE).

q.t: Why are the three angles of an equilateral triangle equal?
o: Each pair of equal sides makes the opposite angles equal
q.e: AB = AC gives ∠C = ∠B; AB = BC gives ∠C = ∠A — so all equal.

q.t: An isosceles triangle has a 40° angle between its equal sides. The other two angles are each…
q.e: The base angles are equal: (180 − 40) ÷ 2 = 70°.

q.t: In the isosceles-angle proof, the altitude AD makes ∆ADB ≅ ∆ADC by…
q.e: Right angles at D, hypotenuses AB = AC, and the shared side AD.

q.t: ∆AIR ≅ ∆FLY. Which angle equals ∠R?
q.e: Third letter matches third letter: R ↔ Y.

q.t: OB = OC and OA = OD where AD and BC cross at O. Why is AB ∥ CD?
o: ∆AOB ≅ ∆DOC, so alternate angles ∠OAB and ∠ODC are equal
Because O is in the middle
q.e: SAS (vertically opposite angles) gives congruent triangles; equal alternate angles on transversal AD mean the lines are parallel.

q.t: In how many ways can an equilateral triangle be placed exactly onto a copy of itself?
q.e: Any vertex can go to any of 3 places, and it can be flipped or not: 3 × 2 = 6.

q.t: An isosceles triangle has base angles of 65°. The angle between the equal sides is…
Square ABCD: in how many ways does ∆ABC fit on ∆ADC (as shown by statements like ∆ABC ≅ ∆ADC and ∆ABC ≅ ∆CDA)?
q.e: All sides of a square are equal, so the triangle can be laid on the other either way round.

q.t: PQ = 6 cm, QR = 4 cm, ∠P = 30°. How many different triangles PQR can be drawn?
q.e: The 4 cm arc from Q cuts the 30° line from P at two points — the SSA case.

q.t: CD ∥ AB and AB = CD, with AD and BC crossing at O. Which rule proves ∆AOB ≅ ∆DOC?
o: ASA — using two pairs of alternate angles
q.e: ∠OAB = ∠ODC and ∠OBA = ∠OCD (alternate angles), with AB = DC between them.

q.t: The kite fact 'AC divides ∠BAD into two equal parts' follows because…
q.e: Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal.

q.t: Can a triangle with sides 5, 5, 5 have an angle of 70°?
q.e: An equilateral triangle's angles are all equal and total 180°.

q.t: Which pair of facts is enough for two right triangles (90° at B and Y) to be congruent?
q.e: Hypotenuse plus one side (RHS). Angles alone can't fix the size.

q.t: An isosceles triangle has one angle of 100°. What are the other two?
q.e: 100° can't be a base angle (two of them would exceed 180°), so it is the top angle: (180 − 100) ÷ 2 = 40°.
